ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory continuous screening must be run against the New Zealand sanctions regime, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, Department of Internal Affairs, and Financial Markets Authority warnings. All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories must be checked for politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates. The protocol requires 100% hit-match independent adjudication, audit trail preservation for at least five years, enhanced due diligence for positive hits or high-risk jurisdictions, and source-of-wealth verification where China-connected ownership, particularly a WFOE, invokes PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 with Government_Only_Access data.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Company Name Reservation Portal, accessible through the Companies Register online service at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed legal names must be entered in Latin-script English and be capable of expression using the letters A to Z, numerals, and the limited punctuation prescribed by the Companies Act 1993. Chinese characters are not accepted in the legal name of a New Zealand company. For any Chinese-language brand associated with the business, a four-tier naming doctrine applies: (1) the registered English legal name, (2) the Chinese commercial name recorded in board minutes, (3) the official pinyin phonetic transliteration, and (4) the corresponding Chinese company registration name in the investor's home jurisdiction. Any mismatch between these tiers must be reconciled by a notarised translation in English before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 20 working days of the rejection notice, the applicant must lodge a written appeal with the Companies Office using the name objection portal, attaching the reservation number, a statutory declaration explaining the distinctive elements of the name, and any registered trade mark or prior-use evidence. The Registrar must issue a reconsideration decision within 15 working days. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972, or submit a fresh application with a materially different name after the 30-day reservation expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in New Zealand must be a physical street address where documents may be legally served during business hours; a post office box or a pure commercial mailbox is not permissible. A virtual office may be accepted by the Companies Office only if it provides a genuine physical street address, a dedicated office suite, and a local service agent physically present to accept service. However, Inland Revenue and banking partners for a cosmetics DTC retail business will generally reject a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox because they require a verifiable trading location, accessible records, and operational substance for GST registration, Shopify Payments, and PayPal merchant accounts. A serviced office with a signed lease, reception services, and demonstrable business presence is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical on-site inspections: on-site signage, accessible reception area, lease or tenancy agreement, utility and internet accounts, physical or digital stock records, staff presence, GST-compliant invoices, payment terminals, and alignment between the registered office and actual operations. Quantified risk: low-to-moderate, estimated at 15-25% annually for this industry if the entity has no physical footprint; the risk rises to 60-75% if the registered office is merely a mailbox, if the principal place of business is outside New Zealand, or if Inland Revenue receives inconsistent reporting. Registrar and Inland Revenue officials may conduct ad hoc verification visits and impose penalties for non-substantive registered office arrangements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), including ss 10-17 (incorporation and name), ss 19-24 (legal capacity and execution), ss 28-31 (constitution), ss 40-46 (share capital and allotment), ss 121-137 (directors and duties), ss 150-151 (consents and disqualification), ss 188-190 (registered office), and ss 199-210 (records and annual return)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Business Registries, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 - Application for Registration of a Company under the Companies Act 1993, filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Register portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand company law does not prescribe any minimum issued or paid-up capital for a company limited by shares. The company may be incorporated with a single share or such number of shares as the subscribers resolve, at any lawful par value, and there is no statutory requirement to maintain a blocked escrow account or to show a minimum paid-up deposit before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FORMAL PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the Company)

Adopted by the unanimous resolution of the directors and the shareholder(s) on [Date], under section 122 of the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), and effective immediately upon incorporation.

BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The subscribers named in the share register hereby subscribe for and are allotted the number of ordinary shares set opposite their respective names in the share register. Each share ranks equally in all respects as to dividends, voting, and return of capital. The board acknowledges receipt from each subscriber of the full issue price in cash or lawful consideration as recorded in the financial ledger, and confirms that no share is issued at a discount. The directors are instructed that any future issue or allotment of shares, options, or convertible securities shall be made only in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, the company's constitution, and the pre-emptive rights of existing shareholders.

2. Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the opening and maintenance of the company's principal operating bank accounts at [Bank Name], [Branch Address], New Zealand. The appointed account signatories shall be [Director 1 Name], [Director 2 Name], and [Director 3 Name] as applicable, and payments shall be made under a dual-signatory mandate for amounts exceeding NZD [threshold]. The board directs that certified copies of the certificate of incorporation and this resolution be provided to the bank as the company's authorizing documentation, and that all online payment systems, payment gateways, and account administrators be linked to the approved bank mandate.

3. Registered Office. The registered office of the company for service of notices and documents shall be [Registered Office Address], New Zealand. This address is a physical address within New Zealand and is not a PO Box. The board directs the company secretary or managing director to notify the Companies Office of the registered office, to maintain the constitution, share register, director consents, certificate of incorporation, minutes, and accounting records at that address, and to ensure that the registered office is staffed or accessible during ordinary business hours.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following persons are appointed to the offices set out opposite their names: [Name] as director and managing director; [Name] as company secretary, if the board determines that a secretary is necessary; and [Name] as compliance and anti-money laundering officer for the purpose of any obliged entity obligations. Each director confirms that they have consented to act, are not disqualified under section 151 of the Companies Act 1993, and will discharge their statutory duties of good faith, care, diligence, and conflict avoidance. The board also authorizes the company secretary to apply for the New Zealand Business Number, IRD number, GST number, and any licenses or notifications required for the company's online retail business.

This resolution is binding on all officers and may be executed as a written resolution of the board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Pre-Incorporation Planning
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZ Companies Office, Business Registries, MBIE (Companies Register name search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search in the Companies Register to confirm that the proposed company name is not identical or confusingly similar to a name already reserved or registered and does not contravene section 11 of the Companies Act 1993. If the board intends to modify any default governance rules, settle and execute the constitution at this stage, naming the company and setting out the share rights and any transfer restrictions. The proposed registered office address in New Zealand must be identified, and the occupier or owner of that address must consent in writing to accept service of documents. Each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner should complete identity verification evidence for the online filing.
required_dossiers: Written consent from registered office provider or owner
Identity verification evidence for each director and shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected, the applicant may immediately submit two alternative names. If the constitution is incomplete, the board may adopt corrective wording and refile before registration. No separate formal appeal is available until after rejection; the applicant can seek informal guidance from the Companies Office contact centre and may apply to the Registrar for a name direction under the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Registration Application and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZ Companies Office, Business Registries, MBIE (online incorporation application)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute Form 2 electronically. The application must state the exact company name, the registered office address, the full legal names and addresses of every director, the share allocation list, and the intended initial share subscription values. Each director must provide a separate signed consent to act, and each subscriber must accept the shares shown in the allotment section. Where the online RealMe credential is used, identity may be verified digitally; otherwise, attach notarized or certified copies of valid passports or national identity cards and recent proof of residential address. All consents and the constitution must be internally consistent with the share capital table and the First Board Resolution before the application is submitted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or holds the application for deficient consent or identity evidence, respond within 20 working days via the Companies Office portal, replace the invalid document, and re-certify the consent. If the query relates to a director's disqualification, remove or replace that director before registration; if identity verification is declined, resubmit notarised copies from a recognized authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission, Fee Payment, and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: NZ Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Business Registries, MBIE (online payment portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed application through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal. The current Companies Office registration fee is approximately NZD 105.50, payable by card or online payment method, which is converted to USD in the financial records at the prevailing bank rate. The Registrar will verify the company name, legal requirements, consents, and address, then issue a digital certificate of incorporation and a New Zealand Business Number. Upon registration the company is a separate legal entity, and the certificate issued under section 16 of the Companies Act 1993 is conclusive evidence of incorporation. Download the certificate, endorse it with the date and company number, and retain it in the corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended, contact the Companies Office support centre, inspect the suspended case messages, and provide the requested corrections within the stated timeline. If the payment was declined or the fee is unpaid, retry the payment gateway; if the Registrar refuses the application, correct the defect and submit a new Form 2 without prejudice to prior documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Statutory Board Governance and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; NZ Companies Office and Inland Revenue for post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board and adopt the First Board Resolution, including approval of share subscriptions, selection of the registered office, opening of bank accounts, signatory authority, and appointment of officers. Ensure all officers sign written consents and that the resolutions are inserted into the company minute book. File any required notices in the Companies Register, apply for an IRD number and GST registration with Inland Revenue, and update the Companies Office record if any director or registered office details have changed. The company should also register the bank account with the local branch, implement the dual-signatory mandate, and prepare the AML/KYC onboarding pack for the corporate bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office later notes that a governance document is inconsistent with the certificate or records, the board may ratify the matter by a subsequent resolution, file an amendment with the Registrar where required, and correct the company records. If a bank rejects the banking authority package, the board may issue a revised signatory list and re-certify the resolution; if an officer ceases to be qualified, replace the officer promptly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to a pure online retail business. For cosmetic product safety, the New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) is the relevant regulator; for any physical premises, the relevant territorial authority and Fire and Emergency New Zealand apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no separate operating licence is required for online retail of cosmetics in New Zealand. If the company imports or manufactures cosmetic products, it must comply with the Cosmetic Products Group Standard 2020 notification and product safety obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (New Zealand), with the local territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 if a resource consent is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not applicable / Exempt. Pure online retail distribution does not require a full EIA or Assessment of Environmental Effects. If the company later constructs a warehouse or enters manufacturing or assembly, the local council will classify the activity as permitted or controlled and may require an AEE under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, volatile organic compound, or hazardous

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department, New Zealand Government; online portal: myIR (secure.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity, the statutory procedure is to apply to Inland Revenue for a New Zealand tax file number using the non-resident company IRD number application form available from the Inland Revenue website; the application must provide certified copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, the registered office address, director/beneficial ownership details, and confirmation of any permanent establishment in New Zealand. Once the IRD number is issued, the same number is used as the GST registration number. GST registration must be completed concurrently through myIR if the entity makes or intends to make taxable supplies in New Zealand exceeding NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or if registering voluntarily to claim input tax credits. An overseas company that is required to register under the Companies Act 1993 on the New Zealand Companies Register must first obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and then complete IRD registration through the Companies Office direct data transfer or myIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. A New Zealand limited company is a separate taxable entity; no check-the-box election or look-through entity election applies to a standard NZ limited company. Hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018 and do not provide elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1986
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any 12-month rolling period for taxable supplies; non-resident suppliers of remote services or low-value goods to New Zealand consumers must register under the offshore supplier registration rules when annual New Zealand consumer supplies exceed NZD 60,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, tax authority API clearance, or anti-fraud digital stamping is required. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL e-invoicing network. GST returns and payments are filed electronically via myIR, and the supplier must issue valid GST tax invoices for taxable supplies above the statutory invoice threshold.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1986, a supply of goods is zero-rated for export where the goods are physically removed from New Zealand and the supplier retains evidence of export within the statutory timeframe; a supply to a non-resident can also be zero-rated where the goods are subsequently exported by the non-resident under the statutory conditions. Qualifying cross-border services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated if the services are performed outside New Zealand or are otherwise covered by the statutory export provisions. For cosmetics online retail, the zero-rating applies only to goods shipped by or on behalf of the supplier to an overseas destination, not to goods delivered in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service Export Entry/Export Declaration submitted electronically by the exporter or licensed customs broker
Signed commercial invoice and packing list with product description and HS classification for cosmetic products
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) evidencing goods departed New Zealand and reached the declared overseas destination
Inward foreign exchange credit/remittance advice from a New Zealand bank evidencing repatriation of export proceeds to a New Zealand bank account
Non-resident customer evidence and overseas delivery address documentation, including purchase order, customer registration, and tracked shipping confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating by requiring the full documentation bundle. If the export or foreign exchange repatriation is not substantiated, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at 15% GST and the exporter must account for GST with use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply, including penalties for lack of reasonable care, unacceptable tax position, gross carelessness, abusive tax position, and evasion, with the maximum penalty for evasion up to 150% of the tax shortfall; willful or reckless false documentation can also give rise to criminal prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ); no separate foreign-exchange-control administration exists because New Zealand maintains a fully floating and freely convertible currency regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand is an open economy with no exchange controls. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible on both current account and capital account transactions, and there are no gatekeeper exchange-control approvals, currency surrender requirements, or repatriation restrictions for ordinary trade and investment flows. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand does not ration foreign currency or impose mandatory buy/sell spreads. A New Zealand limited company may receive shareholder equity, director loans, intercompany advances, and trade receivables in NZD or any foreign currency without central bank permission. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is constrained only by corporate law and tax law: a director-approved solvency test is required for dividend distributions under the Companies Act 1993, and a non-resident dividend withholding tax (NRWT) may apply at the treaty rate, generally 15% unless a Double Tax Agreement reduces it; these are fiscal formalities, not exchange-control restrictions. External debt repayments are likewise free from exchange-control consent. Urgent or unusually high-value capital flows may attract bank enhanced due diligence, anti-money-laundering, and Inland Revenue/CRS reporting, but no economic or administrative convertibility hurdle exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand abolished exchange controls in March 1985. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no requirement to surrender foreign-currency receipts to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or to a local dealer. Exporters may retain balances abroad or in NZ registered bank foreign-currency accounts and may convert at freely negotiated commercial rates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional, medium feasibility for non-custodial payment-clearing flows; low feasibility as a primary company bank or capital-escrow depositary. New Zealand has no separate electronic-money-institution licence; a non-bank fintech cannot accept demand deposits or conduct a deposit-taking business unless it obtains registered-bank status from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Offshore digital EMIs such as global payment platforms may lawfully provide payment facilitation, merchant settlement, and remittance services while acting as FSP-registered reporting entities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, but they are not acceptable sub-custodians of regulatory capital or statutory corporate treasury liquidity. Their solvency, ring-fencing, and oversight structures differ from registered banks, and banks that process their settlements may aggregate consumer and DTC funds in ways that intensify CDD complexity. Therefore, use a Tier-1 local bank for the corporate account, capital escrow, FX hedging, and outbound wire facilities; treat EMIs only as supplemental collection/positivity rails for Shopify/PayPal payouts, subject to a documented risk assessment.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement under the Companies Act 1993 that every director physically attend a branch to open a corporate account, but New Zealand banks typically require at least one executive director or beneficial owner to complete a live customer due-diligence interview, either in-branch or via the bank's approved remote video verification. Remote consular/proxy opening is not a uniform statutory right; it is accepted only when the bank policy permits a New Zealand notary, lawyer, or consular officer to certify identity and authority under an apostilled power of attorney, followed by a recorded confirmation call with the actual signatory. A fully offshore director board will usually face additional documentation requests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity caused by a layered foreign parent structure and non-resident directors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: NZ Companies Office Certificate of Incorporation, current companies register extract, register of shareholdings, signed beneficial-ownership schedule naming every natural person with 25% or greater direct/indirect interest, passport copies and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders, ultimate-parent constitutional documents, and an apostilled/notarised board resolution confirming ownership for account-opening purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingled and high-frequency e-commerce settlement flows from Shopify Payments and PayPal presenting source-of-funds traceability risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant settlement statements from Shopify Payments and PayPal, backend order-level transaction reports mapping customer purchases to settlement batches, refund/chargeback reports, payment-processor compliance policies, e-commerce platform dashboard screenshots, management accounts, and an external accountant's forensic reconciliation letter confirming gross and net receipts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and source-of-wealth concerns arising from non-resident beneficial owners or beauty-supply counterparties connected to higher-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete PEP and sanctions declarations for all shareholders, directors, and signatories; third-party screening results from a reputable provider such as Dow Jones, World-Check, Refinitiv, or LexisNexis; original source-of-funds/source-of-wealth evidence including tax returns, bank statements, employment/business registration, and an independent lawyer's or chartered accountant's certificate confirming the legitimacy of accumulated wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flags through over/under-invoicing, shipment valuation variances, or invoice mismatches in the cosmetics and beauty retail supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed supplier contracts, pro-forma invoices, final commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents such as an air waybill or bill of lading, customs declarations, import/export permits, cargo insurance certificates, proof of payment via SWIFT MT103, and an independent audit certificate confirming that each goods flow is matched to an identical bank payment and recorded in the accounting system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route the cross-border investment by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas investor's bank directly into the NZD corporate account at the selected New Zealand Tier-1 bank. In field 70 (Remittance Information) state 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION NZ' and reference the New Zealand Companies Office company number. No New Zealand exchange-control approval or official foreign-exchange purpose code is required; for bank balance-of-payments reporting the payment should be classified as direct investment in equity capital. The capital-verification package must include the executed shareholder resolution, share subscription agreement, capital contribution booking in the annual accounts, SWIFT confirmation, and a director solvency certificate where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlement, use SWIFT MT103 for direct open-account or advance-payment supplier wires, incorporating invoice numbers and supplier reference numbers in field 70. For high-value or high-risk cosmetic inventory purchases, use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP 600 via MT700, with the beneficiary's presentation including commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, certificate of origin, and insurance certificate. For established trade relationships, Documentary Collections under URC 522 (D/P or D/A terms) provide a lower-cost alternative where the bank forwards shipping documents to the collecting bank against payment or acceptance. All outbound disbursements should match underlying trade contracts and be supported by a periodic external audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts for NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD, NZD/CNH, and NZD/JPY with tenors matched to monthly DTC sales settlement cycles, supported by underlying forecast or contracted receipts.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for non-deliverable emerging-market currencies such as KRW, INR, TWD, or similar immediately convertible-obstacle currencies, executed with a registered bank or approved market counterparty; NDFs are not required or permitted for pure NZD against freely convertible currencies.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps and deliverable FX swaps for term-matching intercompany loans, acquisition funding, or shareholder loans, documented under ISDA/CSA and limited to the verified notional of the balance-sheet exposure.
Zero-cost FX collars and vanilla FX options for non-speculative hedging, subject to a board-approved treasury policy and the bank's credit and risk appetite framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$200 (approx USD 120) and potential removal from register after 30 days notice

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit if company is 'large' (total assets > NZ$60m, revenue > NZ$30m, or 50+ employees) or if shareholders holding 5% or more request an audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (Tier 1/2) for large companies; Simplified Reporting (Tier 3/4) for small companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual return must confirm significant control; any changes to UBO must be filed with the Companies Office within 10 days

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad-based tax holiday exists for online retail trade or DTC cosmetics distribution. The only material corporate incentive is the 15% refundable R&D tax credit for eligible New Zealand research and development expenditure. The imputation credit system prevents double taxation of distributed profits at shareholder level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed electronically through the Inland Revenue myIR secure portal or an approved e-filing gateway.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July of the same calendar year. Taxpayers using a registered tax agent with an extension of time arrangement may file by 31 March of the following income year. Non-standard balance dates follow the approved filing date specified by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross assessable income derived during the income year, including online sales revenue, interest, dividends, foreign-source income, and other taxable income. Shopify and PayPal settlements are reported gross of merchant fees unless separately treated as deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An NZ Ltd is tax resident in New Zealand and must report worldwide income. Foreign-source income may be excluded only where a specific New Zealand tax treaty sourcing rule or active foreign business exemption applies. Apportionment must be supported by contemporaneous records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred in deriving assessable income: cost of goods sold, fulfilment and freight, Shopify/PayPal transaction fees, marketing expenses, salaries, rent, depreciation, interest, and arm's-length related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned companies must not claim notional head-office charges, unsupported royalty allocations, or intra-group management fees unless a transfer pricing analysis demonstrates arm's-length behaviour. Excessive interest deductions are also restricted by thin capitalisation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income less total expenditure. The amount must reconcile to the audited or management financial statements and to the entity's underlying accounting system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconciliation is critical where foreign currency sales, intercompany balances, and payment gateway settlement charges are present. Any unreconciled variance may trigger an IRD risk review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses available to offset current-year taxable income, applied only to the extent permitted by the shareholder continuity rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: New Zealand loss carryforward requires 49% continuity of significant voting and market value interests on an income-year-to-income-year basis. A change in non-resident shareholding requires rebenchmarking before any loss utilisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit after applying loss offsets and after adding back non-deductible expenditure such as fines, capital losses, entertainment expenses above statutory caps, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All related-party transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected before tax is computed. IRD may reconstruct taxable income if the submitted pricing is not arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income multiplied by 28%, less provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax credits, imputation credits, and any eligible R&D tax credit. The resulting amount is the residual income tax or refund due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits are generally not creditable to non-resident shareholders. Repatriation profiling must account for dividend withholding tax rather than relying on imputation credits. Where a non-resident controller holds more than 50%, the entity should verify whether the dividend is imputed or whether a dividend withholding payment mechanism applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of IR4 attracts an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250, with an additional NZD 250 charged after seven days of continued non-filing, followed by further incremental penalties for protracted default. Late payment of residual income tax attracts a late payment penalty of 1% of the unpaid amount on the due date and additional monthly late payment penalties while the debt remains outstanding. Use-of-money interest is also charged daily at the prescribed IRD rate. Shortfall penalties for inaccurate or false returns can range from 20% to 150% of the tax shortfall depending on culpability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders. Under an applicable double tax agreement, the rate is commonly reduced to 15% for portfolio shareholdings and 5% for substantial shareholdings. Fully imputed dividends do not give non-resident shareholders access to imputation credits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must complete an IR290 non-resident withholding tax declaration and provide a current tax residence certificate issued by the competent authority of the treaty jurisdiction. The New Zealand company must receive this documentation before payment, verify beneficial ownership, and confirm that any minimum holding period or substantive ownership condition in the relevant DTA is satisfied. Supporting documentation must be retained for seven years under New Zealand record-keeping requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents attract statutory NRWT of 15%; many New Zealand DTAs reduce the rate to 10%. Interest paid to non-residents also attracts statutory NRWT of 15%, but the rate can be reduced to nil on eligible offshore borrowing if the New Zealand borrower elects to pay the Approved Issuer Levy at 2%. Treaty reductions for interest commonly apply at 10%. Related-party interest and royalties must also satisfy ordinary transfer pricing and thin capitalisation rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Country-by-Country reporting and the associated Master File obligation apply where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds NZD 1.1 billion. A Local File and international dealings disclosure are expected where the New Zealand entity has material cross-border related-party transactions, generally exceeding NZD 10 million in aggregate per transaction category, or where related-party transaction values exceed NZD 5 million and the New Zealand entity has gross income above NZD 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations code comparable to certain offshore financial centres. Instead, New Zealand applies OECD BEPS-aligned principles: corporate residence is determined by incorporation and management/control, loss continuity requires real shareholder identity, treaty access requires beneficial ownership and economic substance, and the general anti-avoidance rule under section BG1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 can disallow artificial arrangements lacking commercial purpose. An online cosmetics retailer must demonstrate genuine New Zealand operational substance, including local management, staff, inventory decision-making, marketing control, and risk management, to sustain treaty benefits and tax residence outcomes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Shopify or PayPal sales revenue, understating e-commerce turnover through manipulated settlement reports, fabricating supplier invoices, inflating loss carryforwards, or knowingly signing an IR4 that understates taxable income to avoid the 28% corporate tax charge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal liability under sections 143A and 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994: imprisonment for up to 5 years for individuals and a fine of up to NZD 50,000; a company is liable to a fine of up to NZD 250,000. Civil shortfall penalties can reach 150% of the evaded tax, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct the filing of false returns may be prosecuted as principals. A Departure Prohibition Order can be issued to prevent travel outside New Zealand. Directors may also be disqualified under the Companies Act 1993 and held personally liable for tax diverted through fraud or sham arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a New Zealand shelf company with no physical premises, no employees, no active retail function, and no board decision-making in New Zealand, while using the entity as a pass-through to access New Zealand treaty benefits, imputation credits, or low-risk online retail credibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement may be voided as a tax avoidance structure under section BG1 of the Income Tax Act 2007, allowing IRD to reconstruct profits and deny treaty benefits. Penalties of 20% to 100% of the tax shortfall apply for unacceptable tax positions and abusive tax positions. The Registrar of Companies may also strike off a company that operates no genuine commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit the entity to operate as a shell can be personally assessed for company tax shortfalls where the corporate form is used as a mere facade. Civil recovery proceedings may be brought under the Criminal Proceeds Recovery Act 2009 to freeze and forfeit assets traceable to contrived arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting non-arm's-length purchase prices for imported cosmetics from a related overseas supplier, paying excessive royalties or management fees to an affiliate in a low-tax jurisdiction, or assuming artificial distribution risks to erode New Zealand taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may adjust pricing under sections GC 6 to GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Shortfall penalties of 40% apply for gross carelessness, increasing to 100% for abusive tax positions, with use-of-money interest on all reassessments. Intentional documentation fraud may trigger criminal tax evasion sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or sign off non-arm's-length pricing with knowledge of the tax advantage may become jointly and severally liable for the resulting shortfall. Serious conduct can lead to criminal prosecution, asset preservation orders, and travel restrictions while investigations are ongoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing customer payments through Shopify Payments or PayPal without implementing a risk-based AML/CFT programme, failing to screen customers against sanctions lists, accepting layered or unexplained third-party settlement payments, or deliberately obscuring beneficial ownership of the e-commerce enterprise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, non-compliance attracts fines of up to NZD 2 million for a company and NZD 1 million for an individual. Breach of the Sanctions Act 2020 can lead to imprisonment for up to 7 years and unlimited fines. Payment processors may also terminate merchant facilities without notice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers of AML/CFT reporting entities can be held personally liable where the breach is attributable to their consent, participation, or neglect. Conviction can result in disqualification from corporate management, financial restitution orders, and restrictions on overseas travel during criminal proceedings.
